$what: Provenance of editor_bg_override.handover-band.json — THE HANDOVER BAND. aeon's live shipped OJZ act-1 background with one 8x4 BgAnim band promoted onto it, authored through Aurora's REAL UI (Effects panel -> From existing tiles -> Promote, saved with a Ctrl+S keystroke) and certified against aeon's OWN injector. This is the file aeon's lane lands as their BGANIM-BAND item; it is a HANDOVER ARTIFACT, not a test fixture with a test bound to it.
$why_it_matters: It is the first BgAnim band that is meant to actually MOVE in the ROM. `phaseFill: 'shift'` is what makes that true: the panel's DEFAULT fill is 'copy', which validates perfectly and is visually inert. Banks 1..7 here are true 1px rolls of phase 0.

band.why_not_insert: planBandInsertion (src/core/formats/bg-override/bg-anim-band.ts) only REMAPS existing layout words (`idx < slotBase ? idx : idx + n`). It never points a layout cell at the new slots, so an inserted band is real in the blob and INVISIBLE on screen. Promotion converts tiles the layout ALREADY draws, so the band is on screen by construction and costs zero new slots.
band.why_tile_2: measured, not chosen: over every 32-tile window of the source blob, `refs * horizontal-edges` is maximised at base 2 (tied with base 3). 1244 of 4096 layout cells (30.4% of the screen) draw that range, 775 horizontal pixel edges, zero flat tiles.
band.why_timer: a timer band animates with the camera still, so the motion is watchable standing in one place
band.rate_shift_note: THE KEY IS ABSENT AND THAT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Aurora's BgAnimBandPanel has NO rate_shift control (it builds its BandSpec from cols/rows/phaseFill/driver only), so a UI-authored band cannot spell it. aeon's own default therefore applies: `a.get('rate_shift', 2)` in tools/inject_editor_bg.py, i.e. step = Logic_Tick >> 2. The emitted band table was read back and says rate_shift=2. If the aeon lane wants a different rate, it is a one-key edit there or a panel control here — it is NOT authorable through Aurora today.

composition_probe.significance: BgAnim_Table goes from the disabled stub to u16 = 1. aeon's ROM has carried band_count = 0 since dd93a840 (2026-07-21); this is the first document that turns it on.
composition_probe.what_it_CANNOT_see: it checks the SIZE of bg_anim_banks.bin, not its contents — a copy-filled INERT band emits exactly 8192 B too. The motion probe below is what closes that.

motion_probe.method: bakes the document through aeon's injector and unpacks the emitted bg_anim_banks.bin in the PACKED 4bpp encoding the ROM DMAs (32 B/tile, 8 rows x 4 bytes, high nibble = even pixel) — independently of Aurora's JSON
motion_probe.emitted_band_table: driver=2 (aeon's DRIVERS['timer'])  rate_shift=2  step_mask=63  col_shift=7  tile_count=32  vram_dest=$8000
motion_probe.result: pattern 64px; bank k == bank 0 rolled k px LEFT for all 8 banks; banks 1..7 all differ from bank 0 -> THE BAND MOVES
motion_probe.encoding_trap: A phase tile in editor_bg_override.json is 64 PIXEL NIBBLES, row-major — NOT 32 packed bytes. Decode it the packed way and every bank reads as broken in a way that looks exactly like a writer defect. The two probes read the two different encodings on purpose.

guard_repointed.was: if (free !== 0) throw new Error('VACUOUS: this document is not full; the point is that it is …')
guard_repointed.why_it_was_right: at 448/448 insertBand refuses at EVERY band size, so promotion was the only door and a roomy document meant the run was on the easy path by accident
guard_repointed.why_it_is_obsolete: aeon's live document was regenerated from a simplified source and is 320/448, so the guard refuses the real file — and asserts nothing about what makes a promotion worth running
guard_repointed.now: counts the layout cells pointing into FROM..FROM+n and refuses at ZERO. A promotion's whole claim is that it converts art the layout ALREADY draws; if nothing draws the range, the run proves nothing however perfectly the bytes validate. Occupancy is still printed and gates nothing.
